name: DFT as computational physics' largest application
summary: Kohn-Sham DFT with plane waves, pseudopotentials, FFTs and iterative eigensolvers is among the most heavily used computational methods in all of science; numerical analysis (basis convergence, k-point sampling, self-consistency mixing) controls its accuracy.
sources: Kresse & Furthmüller (1996). "Efficiency of ab-initio total energy calculations for metals and semiconductors using a plane-wave basis set". *Comput. Mater. Sci.* 6, 15. [doi:10.1016/0927-0256(96)00008-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0927-0256(96)00008-0)

name: Machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on DFT
summary: Neural-network and kernel potentials fitted to DFT energies and forces reach near-DFT accuracy at the cost of classical force fields, enabling million-atom, nanosecond simulations of phase transitions, defects and hydrides.
sources: Behler & Parrinello (2007). "Generalized Neural-Network Representation of High-Dimensional Potential-Energy Surfaces". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 98, 146401. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.146401](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.98.146401)

name: Machine-learned structure predicts glassy dynamics
summary: A machine-learned structural order parameter ('softness') trained on local particle environments predicts which particles in a supercooled liquid will rearrange, connecting hidden structure to dynamical heterogeneity.
sources: Schoenholz et al. (2016). "A structural approach to relaxation in glassy liquids". *Nat. Phys.* 12, 469. [arXiv:1506.07772](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.07772)

name: Neural-network quantum states
summary: Neural networks used as variational wavefunctions (restricted Boltzmann machines, then transformers) are optimized by variational Monte Carlo and now compete with DMRG and QMC on frustrated magnets and the doped Hubbard model.
sources: Carleo & Troyer (2017). "Solving the quantum many-body problem with artificial neural networks". *Science* 355, 602. [arXiv:1606.02318](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.02318)

name: Ab initio molecular dynamics
summary: Car-Parrinello and Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics integrate nuclear motion on DFT forces computed on the fly, unifying electronic structure with MD for liquids, melting and high-pressure phases.
sources: Car & Parrinello (1985). "Unified Approach for Molecular Dynamics and Density-Functional Theory". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 55, 2471. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.2471](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.2471)

name: Molecular dynamics of supercooled liquids and jamming
summary: Simulations of Lennard-Jones and soft-sphere mixtures supply dynamical heterogeneity, the Kauzmann and mode-coupling tests and jamming criticality, but are limited to ~microsecond times, about 10^-6 of the laboratory glass-transition timescale.
sources: Debenedetti & Stillinger (2001). "Supercooled liquids and the glass transition". *Nature* 410, 259. [doi:10.1038/35065704](https://doi.org/10.1038/35065704)

name: Bead-spring simulations of entangled polymers
summary: The Kremer-Grest bead-spring model showed by MD the crossover from Rouse to reptation dynamics in entangled melts and remains the standard coarse-grained test bed for polymer rheology.
sources: Kremer & Grest (1990). "Dynamics of entangled linear polymer melts: A molecular-dynamics simulation". *J. Chem. Phys.* 92, 5057. [doi:10.1063/1.458541](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.458541)

name: Cluster Monte Carlo for magnetic spin models
summary: Critical slowing down in Metropolis simulations of Ising and Heisenberg magnets was beaten by Swendsen-Wang and Wolff cluster updates built on the Fortuin-Kasteleyn mapping; loop and worm algorithms extend this to quantum magnets.
sources: Swendsen & Wang (1987). "Nonuniversal critical dynamics in Monte Carlo simulations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 58, 86. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.86](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.86)

name: Quantum Monte Carlo and the fermion sign problem
summary: Determinant, auxiliary-field and diagrammatic QMC map correlated electrons onto Monte Carlo sampling in imaginary time; for doped fermions and frustrated magnets the weights turn negative and the sign problem makes cost exponential.
sources: Troyer & Wiese (2005). "Computational Complexity and Fundamental Limitations to Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 170201. [arXiv:cond-mat/0408370](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0408370)

name: Entanglement structure of correlated ground states
summary: Area-law entanglement in gapped correlated phases is what makes tensor-network compression possible; deviations (log corrections at criticality, topological entanglement entropy) diagnose the phase.

name: Topological order as an entanglement pattern
summary: Topological order shows up as a constant negative correction to area-law entanglement, the topological entanglement entropy gamma=ln D, and string-net and toric-code ground states are exact PEPS with virtual symmetries; tensor networks thereby identify topological phases numerically.
sources: Levin & Wen (2006). "Detecting Topological Order in a Ground State Wave Function". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 110405. [arXiv:cond-mat/0510613](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0510613)

name: DMRG and tensor networks for correlated electrons
summary: DMRG, invented for quantum spin chains, is a variational method over matrix product states; PEPS, MERA and their 2D cylinder implementations now give benchmark ground states of Hubbard and frustrated spin models, limited by area-law entanglement growth.
sources: Schollwoeck (2011). "The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states". *Ann. Phys.* 326, 96. [arXiv:1008.3477](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.3477)

name: MERA and entanglement at quantum critical points
summary: Critical ground states violate the area law logarithmically; the multiscale entanglement renormalization ansatz (MERA) captures this with a scale-invariant tensor network that implements real-space RG and resembles a discretized AdS geometry.
map: S(\ell)=\frac c3\ln\frac\ell a\ (\text{1+1D CFT});\ \text{MERA layers}\leftrightarrow\text{RG scale}\leftrightarrow\text{radial AdS coordinate}
sources: Vidal (2008). "Class of Quantum Many-Body States That Can Be Efficiently Simulated". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 101, 110501. [arXiv:quant-ph/0610099](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0610099)
Swingle (2012). "Entanglement Renormalization and Holography". *Phys. Rev. D* 86, 065007. [arXiv:0905.1317](https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.1317)

name: Emergence and the limits of reductionism
summary: Anderson's 'More is different' and Laughlin and Pines' 'Theory of Everything' used broken symmetry, quasiparticles and protected quantization in correlated matter as the central examples in the philosophical debate over emergence and reduction.
sources: Anderson (1972). "More Is Different". *Science* 177, 393. [doi:10.1126/science.177.4047.393](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.177.4047.393)
Laughlin & Pines (2000). "The Theory of Everything". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 97, 28. [doi:10.1073/pnas.97.1.28](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.97.1.28)

name: Kramers-Kronig relations for lattice and optical response
summary: Causality makes the dielectric and phonon response functions analytic in the upper half-plane, so absorption and dispersion are Hilbert transforms of each other; this links the TO-phonon resonance, reflectivity and the Lyddane-Sachs-Teller relation.

name: Bloch theorem as Floquet theory of periodic ODEs
summary: Bloch's theorem is Floquet's 1883 theorem for linear differential equations with periodic coefficients; bands and gaps of the Kronig-Penney and nearly-free-electron models are the stability and instability zones of Hill's and Mathieu's equations.

name: Many-body Green's functions and DMFT
summary: Correlated-electron theory is built on Matsubara Green's functions and self-energies; DMFT maps the lattice problem onto an impurity whose local Green's function is fixed self-consistently, an operational use of Dyson's equation.
sources: Georges, Kotliar, Krauth & Rozenberg (1996). "Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated fermion systems and the limit of infinite dimensions". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 68, 13. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.68.13](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.68.13)

name: Bloch bands as an eigenvalue problem
summary: Band structure is the spectral decomposition of a lattice-translation-invariant Hamiltonian: Bloch's theorem block-diagonalizes it by crystal momentum, leaving finite Hermitian matrices H(k) to diagonalize.
map: [H,T_{\mathbf R}]=0\Rightarrow H=\bigoplus_{\mathbf k}H(\mathbf k),\ H(\mathbf k)u_{n\mathbf k}=E_n(\mathbf k)u_{n\mathbf k}

name: Berry curvature as the curvature of a bundle
summary: Berry connection and curvature are a U(1) connection and its curvature on the bundle of Bloch states over the Brillouin-zone torus; the Chern number is the first Chern class and the quantum geometric tensor combines a metric with this curvature.
map:
\mathcal A=i\langle u|duangle,\ \Omega=d\mathcal A,\ C= rac1{2\pi}\int_{T^2}\Omega\in\mathbb Z;\ Q_{\mu
u}=g_{\mu
u}-	frac i2\Omega_{\mu
u}
sources: Simon (1983). "Holonomy, the Quantum Adiabatic Theorem, and Berry's Phase". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 51, 2167. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.51.2167](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.51.2167)

Thouless, Kohmoto, Nightingale & den Nijs (1982). "Quantized Hall Conductance in a Two-Dimensional Periodic Potential". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 405. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.405](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.405)

name: Shot noise and Johnson noise in conductors
summary: The Johnson-Nyquist and Schottky formulas of instrumentation are limits of mesoscopic noise theory: shot noise reduced by the Fano factor sum T(1-T)/sum T, and measuring it revealed the e/3 charge of fractional quantum Hall quasiparticles.
sources: Blanter & Büttiker (2000). "Shot noise in mesoscopic conductors". *Phys. Rep.* 336, 1. [arXiv:cond-mat/9910158](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9910158)
de-Picciotto et al. (1997). "Direct observation of a fractional charge". *Nature* 389, 162. [arXiv:cond-mat/9707289](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9707289)

name: Superconducting cryogenic sensors
summary: Transition-edge sensors, kinetic-inductance detectors and superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors turn the superconducting transition and the small gap into energy-resolving, photon-counting sensors for X-ray, optical and millimetre-wave astronomy and quantum optics.
sources: Irwin (1995). "An application of electrothermal feedback for high resolution cryogenic particle detection". *Appl. Phys. Lett.* 66, 1998. [doi:10.1063/1.113674](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.113674)
Day et al. (2003). "A broadband superconducting detector suitable for use in large arrays". *Nature* 425, 817. [doi:10.1038/nature02037](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02037)

name: SQUIDs as instrumentation
summary: SQUIDs are the most sensitive magnetic-flux detectors and the readout amplifiers of cryogenic sensor arrays; their noise is set by Josephson-junction physics and can approach the quantum limit.

name: Space groups and representations in crystals
summary: The 230 space groups and their irreducible representations label Bloch bands, phonon branches and selection rules, explain systematic absences in diffraction, and the crystallographic restriction (no 5-fold axes) made quasicrystals a surprise.
map: \{R|\mathbf t\}\psi_{n\mathbf k}=\psi_{n,R\mathbf k};\ \text{little group }G_{\mathbf k}\ \text{irreps label bands};\ 2\cos(2\pi/n)\in\mathbb Z
sources: Shechtman et al. (1984). "Metallic Phase with Long-Range Orientational Order and No Translational Symmetry". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 53, 1951. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.1951](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.53.1951)

name: Topological order as broken higher-form symmetry
summary: Generalized (higher-form) global symmetries act on line and surface operators; deconfined topological phases such as the toric code spontaneously break a 1-form symmetry, extending the symmetry-breaking classification of phases to topological order and its mixed-state versions.
sources: Gaiotto, Kapustin, Seiberg & Willett (2015). "Generalized Global Symmetries". *J. High Energy Phys.* 02, 172. [arXiv:1412.5148](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5148)

name: Topological quantum chemistry via band representations
summary: Induced (band) representations of space groups decide whether a set of bands can come from localized symmetric Wannier orbitals; when they cannot, the bands are topological, which turned representation theory into a high-throughput topology classifier.
sources: Bradlyn et al. (2017). "Topological quantum chemistry". *Nature* 547, 298. [arXiv:1703.02050](https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.02050)

name: Altermagnets break time reversal without magnetization
summary: Altermagnets lift Kramers spin degeneracy by breaking the combined time-reversal-plus-translation symmetry of ordinary antiferromagnets while keeping zero net moment, so T-odd responses (anomalous Hall, spin splitting) appear without stray fields.
sources: Krempaský et al. (2024). "Altermagnetic lifting of Kramers spin degeneracy". *Nature* 626, 517. [doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06907-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06907-7)

name: The tenfold way from T, C and chiral symmetry
summary: Gapped free-fermion phases fall into ten Altland-Zirnbauer classes set by whether time reversal T, particle-hole C and chiral S symmetries are present and square to +1 or -1; with dimension this gives the periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors.
sources: Altland & Zirnbauer (1997). "Nonstandard symmetry classes in mesoscopic normal-superconducting hybrid structures". *Phys. Rev. B* 55, 1142. [arXiv:cond-mat/9602137](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9602137)
Kitaev (2009). "Periodic table for topological insulators and superconductors". *AIP Conf. Proc.* 1134, 22. [arXiv:0901.2686](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.2686)

name: Kramers pairs protect topological insulators
summary: The antiunitary time-reversal operator with Theta^2=-1 forces Kramers degeneracy at time-reversal-invariant momenta, giving the Z2 invariant and protecting the surface Dirac cone against non-magnetic backscattering.
sources: Kane & Mele (2005). "Z2 Topological Order and the Quantum Spin Hall Effect". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 146802. [arXiv:cond-mat/0506581](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0506581)

name: Spin-group symmetry classification of altermagnets
summary: Altermagnets are defined by spin-group symmetry, in which spin and lattice operations act independently when spin-orbit coupling is negligible; opposite-spin sublattices related by a rotation rather than a translation or inversion give d-, g- or i-wave spin splitting.
map: [C_2\|C_{4z}]\ \text{(spin flip }\otimes\text{ lattice rotation)}\Rightarrow E_\uparrow(\mathbf k)-E_\downarrow(\mathbf k)\propto k_xk_y
sources: Šmejkal, Sinova & Jungwirth (2022). "Emerging Research Landscape of Altermagnetism". *Phys. Rev. X* 12, 040501. [arXiv:2204.10844](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.10844)

name: Chiral anomaly breaks a Noether current in Weyl semimetals
summary: The axial charge of Weyl fermions is conserved classically by Noether's theorem but not quantum mechanically: parallel E and B pump electrons between Weyl nodes of opposite chirality at the Adler-Bell-Jackiw rate, seen as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance.
sources: Nielsen & Ninomiya (1983). "The Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly and Weyl fermions in a crystal". *Phys. Lett. B* 130, 389. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(83)91529-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(83)91529-0)

name: Magnons as Goldstone bosons and their counting
summary: Magnons are the Goldstone modes of broken spin-rotation symmetry: antiferromagnets have two linearly dispersing type-A modes, while ferromagnets have one quadratic type-B mode because the broken generators have a non-zero commutator expectation; Mermin-Wagner forbids such order in 2D at T>0.
sources: Watanabe & Murayama (2012). "Unified Description of Nambu-Goldstone Bosons without Lorentz Invariance". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 108, 251602. [arXiv:1203.0609](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0609)

Mermin & Wagner (1966). "Absence of Ferromagnetism or Antiferromagnetism in One- or Two-Dimensional Isotropic Heisenberg Models". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 17, 1133. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.17.1133](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.17.1133)

name: Spin liquids: order without symmetry breaking
summary: Quantum spin liquids are the main counterexample to the Landau paradigm: frustration prevents spontaneous symmetry breaking down to T=0, and the low-energy theory instead has emergent gauge fields and fractionalized spinons, so the phase is classified by topology rather than an order parameter.
map: f=|\theta_{CW}|/T_N\gg1;\ \text{no local }\langle\mathbf S_i\rangle\neq0,\ \text{emergent }\mathbb Z_2\text{ or U(1) gauge field}
sources: Balents (2010). "Spin liquids in frustrated magnets". *Nature* 464, 199. [doi:10.1038/nature08917](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature08917)

name: Nematic order, Goldstone modes and homotopy of defects
summary: A nematic breaks rotational symmetry with order-parameter space RP^2; its director fluctuations are Goldstone modes and its defects are classified by homotopy groups, pi_1(RP^2)=Z_2 allowing half-integer disclinations, which is the general topological theory of defects in ordered media.
sources: Mermin (1979). "The topological theory of defects in ordered media". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 51, 591. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.51.591](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.51.591)

name: Superconductivity as broken U(1) gauge symmetry
summary: A superconductor is the condensed-matter Higgs phase: a charged condensate with a phase that breaks U(1), whose would-be Goldstone mode is eaten by the photon, giving the Meissner effect and flux quantization.
sources: Anderson (1963). "Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 439. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.439](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.439)

name: Ginzburg-Landau theory is the abelian Higgs model
summary: The Ginzburg-Landau free energy of a superconductor is, term by term, the static abelian Higgs Lagrangian; the coherence length and penetration depth are the inverse Higgs and photon masses, and kappa=lambda/xi separates type I from type II exactly where Nielsen-Olesen strings attract or repel.
sources: Anderson (1963). "Plasmons, Gauge Invariance, and Mass". *Phys. Rev.* 130, 439. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.130.439](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.130.439)

name: Scaling arguments in polymer physics
summary: Flory's free-energy balance and de Gennes' blob scaling derive polymer size, osmotic pressure and dynamics from dimensional analysis plus a single exponent, a showcase of scaling reasoning without solving the full model.
sources: Flory (1949). "The Configuration of Real Polymer Chains". *J. Chem. Phys.* 17, 303. [doi:10.1063/1.1747243](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1747243)

name: Planckian time from dimensional analysis
summary: At a quantum critical point the only energy scale is temperature, so dimensional analysis gives a relaxation time hbar/k_BT; strange metals saturate this Planckian bound, with measured scattering rates hbar/tau~alpha k_BT and alpha~1.
sources: Zaanen (2004). "Why the temperature is high". *Nature* 430, 512. [doi:10.1038/430512a](https://doi.org/10.1038/430512a)

name: Quantum Hall effect measures the fine-structure constant
summary: von Klitzing introduced the quantized Hall resistance as a determination of alpha, since R_K=h/e^2=mu_0 c/(2 alpha); QHE data entered CODATA adjustments of alpha before the 2019 SI made R_K exact.
sources: von Klitzing, Dorda & Pepper (1980). "New Method for High-Accuracy Determination of the Fine-Structure Constant Based on Quantized Hall Resistance". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 45, 494. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.494](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.494)

name: Graphene quantum Hall resistance standards
summary: Epitaxial graphene on SiC shows wide, robust nu=2 plateaus at higher temperature and lower field than GaAs, allowing table-top quantum resistance standards with part-per-billion accuracy.
sources: Tzalenchuk et al. (2010). "Towards a quantum resistance standard based on epitaxial graphene". *Nat. Nanotechnol.* 5, 186. [arXiv:0909.1220](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.1220)

name: Single-electron pumps and the quantum ampere
summary: Coulomb-blockaded quantum dots and metallic islands clocked at frequency f transfer exactly one electron per cycle, realizing I=ef directly from the fixed elementary charge and closing the quantum metrology triangle with Josephson and quantum Hall standards.
sources: Pekola et al. (2013). "Single-electron current sources: Toward a refined definition of the ampere". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 85, 1421. [arXiv:1208.4030](https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.4030)

name: Josephson voltage standard and the 2019 SI
summary: The AC Josephson effect fixes voltage to frequency through K_J=2e/h exactly; with e and h fixed in the 2019 SI, Josephson arrays realize the volt and, with the Kibble balance, the kilogram.
sources: Josephson (1962). "Possible new effects in superconductive tunnelling". *Phys. Lett.* 1, 251. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0)

name: Quantum Hall resistance standard
summary: Hall plateaus at R_xy=h/(nu e^2) independent of material and geometry realize the ohm via the von Klitzing constant R_K=h/e^2, exact in the 2019 SI.
sources: von Klitzing, Dorda & Pepper (1980). "New Method for High-Accuracy Determination of the Fine-Structure Constant Based on Quantized Hall Resistance". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 45, 494. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.494](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.45.494)

name: Onsager quantization of cyclotron orbits
summary: Quantum oscillations follow from Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization of semiclassical cyclotron orbits on the Fermi surface: the action variable of the orbit fixes allowed k-space areas, so dHvA and SdH frequencies measure extremal Fermi-surface cross sections.
map: J=\oint p\,dq=2\pi\hbar(n+\gamma)\Rightarrow A_k=\frac{2\pi eB}{\hbar}(n+\gamma),\ \Delta(1/B)=\frac{2\pi e}{\hbar A_F}
sources: Onsager (1952). "Interpretation of the de Haas-van Alphen effect". *Phil. Mag.* 43, 1006. [doi:10.1080/14786440908521019](https://doi.org/10.1080/14786440908521019)

name: Berry curvature deforms semiclassical phase space
summary: Semiclassical Bloch electrons with Berry curvature obey non-canonical Hamiltonian dynamics: the anomalous velocity appears and Liouville's phase-space volume is not conserved unless weighted by (1+e B.Omega/hbar), which corrects the density of states.
map: \dot{\mathbf r}=\frac1\hbar\nabla_{\mathbf k}E-\dot{\mathbf k}\times\boldsymbol\Omega,\ \hbar\dot{\mathbf k}=-e(\mathbf E+\dot{\mathbf r}\times\mathbf B);\ D=1+\frac e\hbar\mathbf B\cdot\boldsymbol\Omega
sources: Xiao, Shi & Niu (2005). "Berry Phase Correction to Electron Density of States in Solids". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 137204. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.137204](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.137204)

name: Continuum mechanics of soft materials
summary: Soft matter is described at long wavelengths by continuum theories (viscoelastic fluids, gels, nematic hydrodynamics, granular rheology) built on the conservation laws and constitutive-relation framework of continuum mechanics.

name: Dislocations as topological defects of elastic crystals
summary: Plastic deformation of crystals proceeds by motion of dislocations, line defects labelled by a Burgers vector, whose long-range stress fields are solutions of continuum elasticity; their unbinding drives KTHNY two-dimensional melting.
map: \oint d\mathbf u=\mathbf b;\ \sigma_{\text{screw}}=\frac{\mu b}{2\pi r};\ \tau_{\text{Peierls}}\ll\mu/30\ (\text{ideal strength})
sources: Taylor (1934). "The mechanism of plastic deformation of crystals. Part I.—Theoretical". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 145, 362. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1934.0106](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1934.0106)

name: Elastic waves as long-wavelength acoustic phonons
summary: Acoustic phonon branches at small k are the elastic waves of continuum elasticity: their slopes are the longitudinal and transverse sound speeds fixed by elastic constants, which phonon dispersion measurements determine.

name: Contact mechanics, force chains and the Janssen effect
summary: Static granular packs transmit stress through heterogeneous force chains between Hertzian contacts; frictional wall support saturates pressure with depth in silos (Janssen effect), so granular stress cannot be treated as hydrostatic.
sources: Jaeger, Nagel & Behringer (1996). "Granular solids, liquids, and gases". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 68, 1259. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.68.1259](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.68.1259)

name: Maxwell counting and isostatic jamming
summary: Maxwell's 1864 constraint counting for the rigidity of frames gives the isostatic contact number z=2d at the jamming transition; above jamming, shear modulus and excess contacts grow as power laws of compression.
sources: Maxwell (1864). "On the calculation of the equilibrium and stiffness of frames". *Phil. Mag.* 27, 294. [doi:10.1080/14786446408643668](https://doi.org/10.1080/14786446408643668)
Liu & Nagel (1998). "Jamming is not just cool any more". *Nature* 396, 21. [doi:10.1038/23819](https://doi.org/10.1038/23819)

name: Frank orientational elasticity and liquid-crystal elastomers
summary: Frank theory is an elasticity for the director field (splay, twist, bend) instead of displacements; coupling it to a rubber network gives liquid-crystal elastomers with 'soft elasticity' and large reversible actuation.
breaks: The director is a unit headless vector, so Frank elasticity has topological defects and no restoring force for uniform rotations; a fluid nematic has zero shear modulus, unlike a solid.

name: Rubber elasticity: entropic springs to neo-Hookean solids
summary: Each network strand is an entropic Gaussian spring, so averaging over strands gives the neo-Hookean strain-energy function of finite-strain continuum elasticity with shear modulus n k_B T, explaining why rubber stiffens on heating.
sources: Treloar & Montgomery (1949). "The physics of rubber elasticity". *Phys. Today*. [doi:10.1063/1.3060678](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3060678)

name: Topological mechanics of isostatic lattices
summary: Band topology applied to the compatibility matrix of Maxwell (isostatic) lattices predicts floppy zero modes localized on particular edges, an index theorem for mechanical metamaterials analogous to the SSH chain.
map: N_0-N_S=dN-N_B;\ \text{topological polarization }\mathbf R_T=\sum_i n_i\mathbf a_i\ (\text{winding of }\det C(\mathbf k))
sources: Kane & Lubensky (2014). "Topological boundary modes in isostatic lattices". *Nat. Phys.* 10, 39. [arXiv:1308.0554](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0554)

name: Electron hydrodynamics in graphene
summary: When electron-electron collisions dominate over impurity and phonon scattering, electrons in clean graphene flow as a viscous fluid obeying Navier-Stokes-like equations, producing negative nonlocal resistance from backflow whirlpools and Poiseuille profiles.
sources: Bandurin et al. (2016). "Negative local resistance caused by viscous electron backflow in graphene". *Science* 351, 1055. [doi:10.1126/science.aad0201](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aad0201)

name: mu(I) rheology: granular matter as a viscoplastic fluid
summary: Dense granular flows obey a local friction law in which the effective friction depends on the inertial number; inserted into continuum momentum equations it predicts flows on inclines, in silos and in rotating drums.
sources: Jop, Forterre & Pouliquen (2006). "A constitutive law for dense granular flows". *Nature* 441, 727. [doi:10.1038/nature04801](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature04801)

name: Nematodynamics: anisotropic viscous flow
summary: Ericksen-Leslie theory couples the Navier-Stokes equations to director rotation, giving three Miesowicz viscosities, flow alignment and backflow; it controls display switching times and active-nematic hydrodynamics.
sources: Leslie (1968). "Some constitutive equations for liquid crystals". *Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal.* 28, 265. [doi:10.1007/BF00251810](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00251810)

name: Electroconvection in nematics
summary: Above a threshold voltage nematic layers develop convection rolls (Williams domains) through the Carr-Helfrich mechanism, an anisotropic analogue of Rayleigh-Benard convection and a classic system for pattern formation and spatiotemporal chaos.
sources: Cross & Hohenberg (1993). "Pattern formation outside of equilibrium". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 65, 851. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.65.851](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.65.851)

name: Colloids, polymers and swimmers in Stokes flow
summary: Soft-matter dynamics is overdamped: colloid diffusion, polymer Rouse-Zimm dynamics and microswimming are governed by Stokes drag and long-range hydrodynamic interactions (Oseen tensor).
map: \mathbf F=6\pi\mu a\mathbf U,\ \mathsf O(\mathbf r)=\frac{1}{8\pi\mu r}(\mathbb 1+\hat{\mathbf r}\hat{\mathbf r})

name: Microswimmers at low Reynolds number
summary: Bacteria and synthetic swimmers live at Re~1e-5, where Purcell's scallop theorem forbids reciprocal strokes and Stokesian far fields (pusher/puller force dipoles) set their collective hydrodynamics and active stresses.
map: \mu\nabla^2\mathbf u=\nabla p,\ \mathbf u_{\text{dipole}}\propto\frac{p}{8\pi\mu r^2}[3(\hat{\mathbf e}\cdot\hat{\mathbf r})^2-1]\hat{\mathbf r}
sources: Marchetti et al. (2013). "Hydrodynamics of soft active matter". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 85, 1143. [arXiv:1207.2929](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.2929)

name: Stokes drag and diffusion of colloids
summary: Colloid diffusion follows from Stokes drag via the Einstein relation, and sedimentation, hydrodynamic interactions and lubrication forces between colloids are low-Reynolds-number flow problems.

name: Active turbulence versus inertial turbulence
summary: Dense bacterial suspensions and active nematics show chaotic mesoscale vortices with power-law energy spectra at Reynolds numbers far below 1, driven by active stress rather than inertia.
map: E(k)\sim k^{-5/3}\ (\text{Kolmogorov, inertial})\ \text{vs}\ E(k)\ \text{power laws set by active length }\ell_a=\sqrt{K/|\zeta|}
breaks: Energy is injected at every scale by active stress and dissipated by viscosity, with no inertial cascade; the vortex size is set by an active length, and spectral exponents are not universal.
sources: Wensink et al. (2012). "Meso-scale turbulence in living fluids". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 109, 14308. [doi:10.1073/pnas.1202032109](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1202032109)

name: Polymer drag reduction and elastic turbulence
summary: Dilute long polymers reduce turbulent drag by up to ~80% (Toms effect) by suppressing near-wall vortices, and in viscous flows polymer elasticity alone drives chaotic 'elastic turbulence' at Reynolds numbers far below 1.
sources: Groisman & Steinberg (2000). "Elastic turbulence in a polymer solution flow". *Nature* 405, 53. [doi:10.1038/35011019](https://doi.org/10.1038/35011019)

name: Inelastic collisions and granular gases
summary: Grains collide with a restitution coefficient below 1, so a granular gas loses energy in every collision; the resulting homogeneous cooling (Haff's law) and clustering instability follow from momentum conservation with kinetic-energy loss.
sources: Haff (1983). "Grain flow as a fluid-mechanical phenomenon". *J. Fluid Mech.* 134, 401. [doi:10.1017/S0022112083003419](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0022112083003419)

name: Chaotic billiards and mesoscopic conductance fluctuations
summary: Ballistic quantum dots whose classical shape gives chaotic trajectories show universal conductance fluctuations and weak-localization lineshapes governed by random-matrix theory, while regular (integrable) shapes do not; classical chaos thus controls quantum transport statistics.
sources: Marcus et al. (1992). "Conductance fluctuations and chaotic scattering in ballistic microstructures". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 69, 506. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.506](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.506)

name: Frenkel-Kontorova model and the standard map
summary: Ground states of the Frenkel-Kontorova model of an incommensurate adsorbate or modulated crystal correspond to orbits of an area-preserving twist map; Aubry's pinning transition, where the incommensurate phase locks to the lattice, is the breakup of a KAM torus, and the devil's staircase of commensurate phases follows.
sources: Aubry (1983). "The twist map, the extended Frenkel-Kontorova model and the devil's staircase". *Physica D* 7, 240. [doi:10.1016/0167-2789(83)90129-X](https://doi.org/10.1016/0167-2789(83)90129-X)

name: FPUT anharmonic lattice and the discovery of solitons
summary: The 1955 Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou simulation of an anharmonic atomic chain failed to thermalize its phonon modes; Zabusky and Kruskal's continuum limit, the KdV equation, explained the recurrence and introduced the soliton.
sources: Zabusky & Kruskal (1965). "Interaction of 'Solitons' in a Collisionless Plasma and the Recurrence of Initial States". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 15, 240. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.15.240](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.15.240)

name: Magnetic skyrmions as topological solitons
summary: Skyrmions are localized, particle-like solutions of the nonlinear micromagnetic field equations, stable because of an integer winding number, the topological-soliton class first introduced by Skyrme for nucleons.
sources: Nagaosa & Tokura (2013). "Topological properties and dynamics of magnetic skyrmions". *Nat. Nanotechnol.* 8, 899. [doi:10.1038/nnano.2013.243](https://doi.org/10.1038/nnano.2013.243)

name: Fluxons in long Josephson junctions are sine-Gordon solitons
summary: The phase difference along a long Josephson junction obeys the sine-Gordon equation; its kink solitons are fluxons carrying one flux quantum, which move relativistically at the Swihart velocity and underlie flux-flow oscillators.

name: SSH domain-wall solitons and topological zero modes
summary: Domain walls between the two dimerization patterns of polyacetylene are solitons that bind a mid-gap zero mode with fractional charge or reversed spin-charge relation; the SSH chain is now the prototype 1D topological insulator (Jackiw-Rebbi index).
sources: Su, Schrieffer & Heeger (1979). "Solitons in Polyacetylene". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 42, 1698. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.42.1698](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.42.1698)

name: Flocking as synchronization in space
summary: Alignment of headings in the Vicsek model is Kuramoto-like phase synchronization of self-propelled oscillators, with the twist that particles move and so couplings change; both show noise-driven order-disorder transitions.
breaks: Vicsek particles move, so the coupling network changes with the order itself, giving density bands and giant number fluctuations that have no counterpart in fixed-network Kuramoto models; their order parameter is a vector, not a phase.
sources: Vicsek et al. (1995). "Novel Type of Phase Transition in a System of Self-Driven Particles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 1226. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1226)

name: Synchronization of Josephson-junction arrays
summary: Series arrays of current-biased junctions coupled through a shared load map onto the Kuramoto model and phase-lock, the route to coherent microwave emission; Shapiro steps are Arnold-tongue frequency locking of a junction to an external drive.
sources: Wiesenfeld, Colet & Strogatz (1996). "Synchronization Transitions in a Disordered Josephson Series Array". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 76, 404. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.404](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.404)

name: Phonons as quantized normal modes
summary: Phonons are the quantized normal modes of the crystal's coupled harmonic oscillators; each mode contributes hbar*omega(n+1/2), giving Debye and Einstein heat capacities.

name: Normal-mode analysis behind lattice dynamics
summary: Translation symmetry turns the classical normal-mode problem of N coupled oscillators into Bloch-labelled branches, the same diagonalization used for electrons in periodic potentials.

name: Monatomic and diatomic chains to phonon branches
summary: The dispersion of a mass-spring chain is the phonon dispersion of a 1D crystal; a two-atom basis splits it into acoustic and optical branches with a gap at the zone boundary, and the dynamical matrix generalizes this to 3D.

name: Mechanical topological insulators from coupled oscillators
summary: Arrays of coupled pendula or resonators engineered to mimic a quantum spin Hall Hamiltonian show helical edge modes, demonstrating that band topology is a property of linear wave equations, not of electrons.
map: \ddot{\mathbf x}=-D\mathbf x,\ D(\mathbf k)\simeq\omega_0^2\mathbb 1+H_{\text{BHZ}}(\mathbf k);\ \omega^2\leftrightarrow E
sources: Süsstrunk & Huber (2015). "Observation of phononic helical edge states in a mechanical topological insulator". *Science* 349, 47. [doi:10.1126/science.aab0239](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aab0239)

name: Drude and Lorentz models as damped driven oscillators
summary: The optical conductivity of metals (free carriers) and insulators (bound oscillators, phonons, excitons) is the response of a driven damped harmonic oscillator, with resonance width set by scattering rate.

name: Phononic crystals: Bloch bands for sound
summary: Periodic elastic composites have acoustic band structures and complete band gaps computed with Bloch's theorem, the classical-wave analogue of electronic band theory that underlies acoustic metamaterials.
map: \mathbf u(\mathbf r+\mathbf R)=e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf R}\mathbf u(\mathbf r);\ \text{gap at }k=\pi/a\ \text{when impedance contrast }Z_1\neq Z_2
sources: Kushwaha et al. (1993). "Acoustic band structure of periodic elastic composites". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 2022. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.71.2022](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.71.2022)

name: Josephson junction as a driven nonlinear pendulum
summary: In the RCSJ model the junction phase is a damped, driven pendulum, giving hysteresis, Shapiro steps and chaos; pumping its nonlinear inductance makes a Duffing-type parametric amplifier used for quantum-limited readout.

name: Magnetization precession as gyroscopic motion
summary: The Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation is the torque equation of a gyroscope for spin angular momentum: the magnetization precesses about the effective field and relaxes through Gilbert damping, while spin-transfer torque acts as an additional applied torque.
map: \frac{d\mathbf M}{dt}=-\gamma\mathbf M\times\mathbf H_{\text{eff}}+\frac\alpha M\mathbf M\times\frac{d\mathbf M}{dt}\leftrightarrow\boldsymbol\tau=\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf L
sources: Gilbert (2004). "A phenomenological theory of damping in ferromagnetic materials". *IEEE Trans. Magn.* 40, 3443. [doi:10.1109/TMAG.2004.836740](https://doi.org/10.1109/TMAG.2004.836740)

name: Einstein-de Haas and Barnett effects
summary: Reversing a ferromagnet's magnetization makes the free body rotate (Einstein-de Haas), and rotating a body magnetizes it (Barnett), because total spin plus rigid-body angular momentum is conserved; these measured the electron g-factor and now enable ultrafast demagnetization studies.

name: Coherent backscattering, speckle and weak localization
summary: Time-reversed paths in a disordered medium interfere constructively. For light this gives the coherent-backscattering cone; for electrons it gives the weak-localization correction to the resistance. Universal conductance fluctuations are electronic speckle, a sample-specific fingerprint. Hanbury Brown–Twiss correlations reappear as electron antibunching and shot noise.
breaks: Light has no Fermi statistics, and for it absorption and moving scatterers play the role of dephasing. 3D Anderson localization of light has not been convincingly shown, and claims for TiO2 powders are contested.

name: The phase problem: crystallography and phase retrieval
summary: A far-field diffraction pattern is the squared Fourier transform of the scattering density, so the phase is lost. Crystallography's Patterson and direct methods and optics' iterative phase retrieval (Gerchberg–Saxton, Fienup) attack the same problem. Combined with oversampling they gave coherent diffractive imaging at synchrotrons and XFELs, and Gabor invented holography for electron microscopy.
map: I(\mathbf q)=|\tilde\rho(\mathbf q)|^2\Leftrightarrow P(\mathbf r)=\int\rho(\mathbf r')\rho(\mathbf r'+\mathbf r)\,d^3r'

name: Electron optics: Snell's law and Veselago lens at p–n junctions
summary: Ballistic Dirac electrons crossing a graphene p–n junction refract according to Snell's law with an effective index ∝ ±k_F. On the hole side the index is negative, so a p–n junction acts as a Veselago lens (Cheianov–Fal'ko–Altshuler). Klein tunnelling sets the angle-dependent transmission, and focusing has been seen in hBN-encapsulated devices.
breaks: λ_F is comparable to device features, so ray optics is only approximate. Smooth junctions collimate electrons toward normal incidence instead of imaging. Pseudospin conservation (Klein tunnelling) has no optical counterpart, and disorder and electron–electron scattering limit coherence.
sources: Castro Neto et al. (2009). "The electronic properties of graphene". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 81, 109. [arXiv:0709.1163](https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1163)

name: SQUID double slit and Josephson Fraunhofer pattern
summary: A DC SQUID is a two-slit interferometer for the condensate, and the critical current of one wide junction in a field follows the single-slit Fraunhofer pattern. In general I_c(Φ) is the modulus of the Fourier transform of the critical-current density J_c(x), and Fourier-optics inversion (Dynes–Fulton) uses this to image supercurrent paths.
breaks: The phase belongs to a macroscopic condensate, not to a light field, and the junction dynamics are nonlinear. The pattern is distorted by self-screening (β_L≳1) and by a Josephson length λ_J shorter than the junction. The measured quantity is a critical current, not an intensity.
sources: Josephson (1962). "Possible new effects in superconductive tunnelling". *Phys. Lett.* 1, 251. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0)

name: Electron quantum optics with quantum Hall edge channels
summary: Chiral quantum Hall edge channels serve as lossless one-way beam paths and quantum point contacts as tunable beam splitters. Together they build electronic Mach–Zehnder and Fabry–Pérot interferometers, which show Aharonov–Bohm oscillations and electronic Hanbury Brown–Twiss and Hong–Ou–Mandel effects. Fabry–Pérot interferometry has also measured the braiding phase of ν=1/3 anyons.
breaks: Electrons are fermions, so they antibunch and obey Pauli exclusion. Coulomb charging effects dominate small Fabry–Pérot devices, and interactions between edge channels cause dephasing and energy relaxation, which limit visibility in a way photons do not.

name: Neumann's principle: crystal system fixes optical class
summary: The dielectric tensor must be invariant under the crystal's point group. Cubic crystals are optically isotropic; tetragonal, trigonal and hexagonal ones are uniaxial; orthorhombic, monoclinic and triclinic ones are biaxial. Birefringence and the optic axes therefore act as structural probes, as in polarizing microscopy of minerals.

name: Valley-selective circular dichroism in TMD monolayers
summary: Broken inversion in MoS2- and WSe2-type monolayers gives opposite Berry curvature and orbital moment at the K and K' valleys. With C3 symmetry this makes σ+ light excite only K and σ− only K'. Helicity therefore writes and reads valley polarization (valleytronics) and reveals the valley Zeeman splitting.

name: Magneto-optics: Faraday and Kerr rotation read M
summary: Magnetization makes the dielectric tensor gyrotropic, with an antisymmetric off-diagonal part proportional to M. The two circular polarizations then see different indices, rotating linear polarization in transmission (Faraday) and reflection (MOKE). Kerr microscopy images domains and skyrmions, and garnet ferrimagnets are used in optical isolators.

name: Nematics as field-switchable birefringent wave plates
summary: A nematic is a uniaxial birefringent medium with its optic axis along the director. Jones-calculus retardation between crossed polarizers, switched by the field-driven Fréedericksz transition, is how every LCD works. Cholesterics add selective Bragg reflection of one circular polarization, and q-plates with a patterned director imprint Pancharatnam–Berry phases.

name: Quantized conductance as electron-waveguide mode counting
summary: In the Landauer–Büttiker picture a point contact is an electron waveguide. Each transverse mode that rises above cutoff as the contact widens adds 2e²/h to the conductance, just as TE/TM modes open in a metal waveguide.
breaks: Electrons are fermions filled up to E_F, so only modes at the Fermi energy carry current and the contact resistance h/(2e²N) is intrinsic. Spin degeneracy and interactions (the 0.7 anomaly) have no counterpart in a lossless EM waveguide.
sources: van Wees et al. (1988). "Quantized conductance of point contacts in a two-dimensional electron gas". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 60, 848. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.60.848](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.60.848)
Landauer (1957). "Spatial Variation of Currents and Fields Due to Localized Scatterers in Metallic Conduction". *IBM J. Res. Dev.* 1, 223. [doi:10.1147/rd.13.0223](https://doi.org/10.1147/rd.13.0223)

name: Graphene's universal πα absorption
summary: Interband transitions of massless Dirac electrons give a frequency-independent sheet conductivity e²/4ħ. Putting it into the Fresnel transmission of a conducting sheet shows that a suspended monolayer absorbs πα≈2.3% of visible light, so a transmission measurement reads off the fine-structure constant.

name: Long Josephson junction as a superconducting stripline
summary: A long Josephson junction is a parallel-plate transmission line that carries a slow Swihart mode. Its nonlinear phase obeys the sine-Gordon equation, whose kink solitons are fluxons each carrying one flux quantum. Superconducting coplanar resonators and junction-embedded transmission lines are the microwave hardware of circuit QED and traveling-wave parametric amplifiers.
sources: Josephson (1962). "Possible new effects in superconductive tunnelling". *Phys. Lett.* 1, 251. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0)

name: Axion electrodynamics in topological insulators
summary: A 3D topological insulator adds a θE·B term to the Maxwell Lagrangian, with θ=π fixed by time reversal. This gives a quantized magnetoelectric effect, image magnetic monopoles and a half-quantized surface Hall conductance once T is broken at the surface. THz Faraday and Kerr rotations quantized in units of α are the observable signature.
map: \mathcal L_\theta=\frac{\theta e^2}{2\pi h}\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B,\ \theta=\pi,\ \sigma_{xy}^{\rm surf}=\frac{e^2}{2h}
sources: Qi & Zhang (2011). "Topological insulators and superconductors". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 1057. [arXiv:1008.2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.2026)
Hasan & Kane (2010). "Colloquium: Topological insulators". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 82, 3045. [arXiv:1002.3895](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.3895)

name: Emergent electromagnetism of skyrmions
summary: A conduction electron whose spin follows a magnetic texture picks up a Berry phase that acts as an emergent vector potential. Each skyrmion carries one emergent flux quantum h/e, which produces the topological Hall effect, and moving skyrmions induce an emergent electric field.

name: London equation: the vector potential gives the photon a mass
summary: In a superconductor the supercurrent is proportional to the vector potential, which is gauge invariant only once the condensate phase gradient is included. Combined with Ampère's law this expels B over the London depth (the Meissner effect): a frequency-independent counterpart of the skin depth, and the condensed-matter case of the Anderson–Higgs mechanism.
sources: Meissner & Ochsenfeld (1933). "Ein neuer Effekt bei Eintritt der Supraleitfähigkeit". *Naturwissenschaften* 21, 787. [doi:10.1007/BF01504252](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01504252)
Bardeen, Cooper & Schrieffer (1957). "Theory of Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 108, 1175. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.108.1175)

name: Gauge-invariant phase difference and flux quantization
summary: Josephson physics depends on the gauge-invariant phase difference, in which the line integral of the vector potential enters as an Aharonov–Bohm-type phase. Fluxoid quantization in units of h/2e follows, and so does the fact that SQUIDs read out the loop integral of A. The AC Josephson relation ties voltage to frequency, which is the basis of the voltage standard.
sources: Josephson (1962). "Possible new effects in superconductive tunnelling". *Phys. Lett.* 1, 251. [doi:10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0](https://doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(62)91369-0)

name: Chiral anomaly driven by the invariant E·B
summary: Parallel E and B pump charge between Weyl nodes of opposite chirality at a rate set by the Lorentz invariant E·B (the dual-field invariant of covariant electrodynamics), through the chiral lowest Landau level. This is the Adler–Bell–Jackiw anomaly in a crystal (Nielsen–Ninomiya), and it predicts negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, which current-jetting artefacts complicate.
sources: Xu et al. (2015). "Discovery of a Weyl fermion semimetal and topological Fermi arcs". *Science* 349, 613. [arXiv:1502.03807](https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03807)

name: Magnetostatic energy, demagnetizing fields and domains
summary: Describing a magnetized body by its bound magnetic charges and currents gives the demagnetizing field and its dipolar self-energy. That energy produces shape anisotropy and, balanced against exchange and crystalline anisotropy, breaks ferromagnets into domains and stabilizes bubble and dipolar-skyrmion textures.
map: \mathbf H_d=-N\mathbf M,\ E_d=-\frac{\mu_0}{2}\int\mathbf M\cdot\mathbf H_d\,dV,\ \rho_m=-\nabla\cdot\mathbf M

name: Coulomb blockade from dot capacitance
summary: Adding one electron to a quantum dot costs the charging energy e²/2C. C and the dot–gate capacitance matrix come from electrostatic boundary-value problems, and gate-defined dots are designed with Poisson/Laplace solvers. Blockade needs E_C≫k_BT and tunnel resistances well above h/e², and the capacitances set the shape of the Coulomb diamonds.
map: E_C=\frac{e^2}{2C},\ C_{\rm disk}=8\epsilon r,\ k_BT\ll E_C,\ R_t\gg h/e^2
sources: Hanson et al. (2007). "Spins in few-electron quantum dots". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 79, 1217. [arXiv:cond-mat/0610433](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0610433)

name: Drude: one response function for optics and DC transport
summary: The Drude permittivity of fields-in-matter and the Drude conductivity of transport are the same causal response function. The DC resistivity, the plasma edge in reflectivity and the free-carrier absorption are three views of it. Kramers–Kronig relations and the f-sum rule let infrared spectra be read as transport.

name: Lorentz oscillator = polar optical phonon (LST relation)
summary: The Lorentz-oscillator permittivity of an ionic crystal is the response of its polar optical phonons. The macroscopic field splits LO from TO modes (Lyddane–Sachs–Teller relation), gives total reflection in the reststrahlen band between them, and mixes phonons with photons into phonon-polaritons.
